name: Plato
summary: Athenian philosopher whose Republic defines justice as each class doing its own work in a state ruled by philosopher-kings.
note: Birth is given as 428 or 427 BCE, death as 348 or 347 BCE.

name: Aristotle
summary: Greek philosopher, Plato's pupil, who called man a political animal by nature and classified constitutions.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; IGNOU Political Science Paper 2

name: Kautilya
summary: Ancient Indian theorist of statecraft credited with the Arthashastra, the saptanga theory of the state and the mandala theory of interstate relations.
note: Dates are uncertain; tradition makes him the minister of Chandragupta Maurya, 4th century BCE.

name: Niccolò Machiavelli
summary: Florentine thinker who separated politics from conventional morality and advised rulers how to gain and keep power.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Jean Bodin
summary: French jurist who gave the first systematic theory of sovereignty as the absolute and perpetual power of a commonwealth.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Thomas Hobbes
summary: English philosopher who argued that people escape a war-like state of nature by a social contract that creates an absolute sovereign.

name: John Locke
summary: English liberal who held that government rests on consent and exists to protect natural rights to life, liberty and property.

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
summary: Genevan philosopher who based legitimate authority on the general will of the sovereign people.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 2; O.P. Gauba

name: John Stuart Mill
aliases: J. S. Mill|J.S. Mill|John S. Mill|Mill
summary: English liberal who defended individual liberty, representative government and the equality of women.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Karl Marx
summary: German thinker who explained history through class struggle and saw the state as an instrument of the ruling class.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Vladimir Lenin
summary: Russian revolutionary who led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 and explained imperialism as the highest stage of capitalism.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 2; O.P. Gauba

name: Max Weber
summary: German sociologist who defined the state by its monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force and classified types of legitimate authority.

name: Antonio Gramsci
summary: Italian Marxist who explained class rule through hegemony, the consent won in civil society alongside coercion.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Harold Laski
summary: British political theorist who argued for a pluralist state that shares sovereignty with other associations.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Hannah Arendt
summary: German-American theorist of totalitarianism and of political action in a shared public realm, who separated power from violence.

name: Isaiah Berlin
summary: British liberal philosopher who distinguished negative liberty from positive liberty and defended value pluralism.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
summary: French existentialist feminist who argued that society makes woman man's Other.

name: John Rawls
summary: American philosopher whose theory of justice as fairness revived liberal political philosophy.

name: Robert Nozick
summary: American libertarian who defended a minimal state and an entitlement theory of justice against Rawls.

name: Amartya Sen
summary: Indian economist and philosopher who judges justice and development by people's real capabilities and freedoms.

name: Michael Walzer
summary: American communitarian thinker who argues that each social good should be distributed by its own criteria.

name: Joseph Schumpeter
summary: Austrian-American economist who redefined democracy as competition between leaders for the people's vote.

name: Robert Dahl
summary: American political scientist of pluralism who called real-world democracies polyarchies.

name: Jürgen Habermas
summary: German philosopher of the public sphere and communicative action, central to deliberative democracy.

name: David Easton
summary: Canadian-American political scientist who built systems analysis and led the post-behavioural revolution.

name: Gabriel Almond
summary: American political scientist who developed the structural-functional approach and the study of political culture.

name: Steven Lukes
summary: British theorist who argued that power has three dimensions, including the shaping of people's wants.

name: Ralph Miliband
summary: British Marxist who saw the capitalist state as serving the ruling class, an instrumentalist view he debated with Poulantzas.

name: Hamza Alavi
summary: Pakistani Marxist scholar who described the post-colonial state as overdeveloped and relatively autonomous of the propertied classes.

name: Friedrich Hayek
summary: Austrian-British economist who argued that central planning destroys liberty and defended the free market and the rule of law.

name: Maurice Duverger
summary: French political scientist who classified parties and party systems and linked electoral systems to the number of parties.

name: Rajni Kothari
summary: Indian political scientist who described the Congress system of one-party dominance and the politicisation of caste.

name: Hans Morgenthau
summary: German-American founder of classical realism, who saw international politics as a struggle for power.

name: E. H. Carr
summary: British historian whose attack on interwar utopianism opened the realist-idealist debate in international relations.

name: Kenneth Waltz
summary: American founder of neorealism, who explained state behaviour by the anarchic structure of the international system.

name: John Mearsheimer
summary: American theorist of offensive realism, who holds that great powers maximise relative power and seek hegemony.

name: Robert Keohane
summary: American theorist of neoliberal institutionalism and, with Joseph Nye, of complex interdependence.

name: Joseph Nye
summary: American liberal scholar of international relations who coined soft power and, with Keohane, developed complex interdependence.

name: Alexander Wendt
summary: American constructivist who argued that anarchy and power politics are shaped by the identities states construct.

name: Immanuel Wallerstein
summary: American sociologist who founded world-systems theory.

name: David Mitrany
summary: Romanian-born British scholar who founded functionalism in international relations.

name: Samuel Huntington
summary: American political scientist known for the clash of civilizations thesis and for work on political order and democratisation.

name: Francis Fukuyama
summary: American political scientist who argued that the triumph of liberal democracy after the Cold War marked the end of history.

name: Woodrow Wilson
summary: US President whose Fourteen Points and League of Nations shaped the idealist approach to international relations.

name: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
aliases: Syed Ahmad Khan|Sir Syed Ahmed Khan|Sir Syed
summary: Muslim reformer who urged modern education and loyalty to British rule and founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh.
note: IGNOU gives 1817-1898 in one unit and 1817-99 in another.

name: Sri Aurobindo
summary: Extremist nationalist turned spiritual philosopher who saw the nation as divine and set out the doctrine of passive resistance.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
summary: Leader of the national movement whose thought rests on truth, non-violence, satyagraha, swaraj and trusteeship.
verified: books: Heywood; IGNOU Political Science Paper 2

name: B. R. Ambedkar
summary: Dalit leader and chair of the Drafting Committee who fought caste through law, rights and social democracy.
note: IGNOU gives 14 April 1891; Austin's Constituent Assembly table prints 1893.
verified: books: Austin; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: M. N. Roy
summary: Early Indian communist who broke with Marxism and founded radical humanism.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: First Prime Minister of India, who shaped non-alignment, Panchsheel and planned development.

name: A. R. Desai
summary: Indian Marxist sociologist who explained nationalism through the economic and class changes of colonial rule.

name: Granville Austin
summary: American historian of the Indian Constitution, who called it first and foremost a social document.

name: K. C. Wheare
summary: Australian-born constitutional scholar who defined the federal principle and called the Indian Constitution quasi-federal.

name: The Republic
summary: Dialogue that defines justice as each of three classes doing its own work, with philosopher-kings ruling the ideal state.

name: Politics
summary: Treatise that classifies constitutions by who rules and for whose good, and favours polity as the best practicable state.

name: Arthashastra
summary: Treatise on statecraft, economy and diplomacy covering the seven limbs of the state, the duties of the king and the circle of states.
note: Its date is debated; tradition places it in the 4th century BCE, many scholars later.
verified: books: Baylis & Smith; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: The Prince
summary: Advice to a new prince on gaining and holding power, using force and deceit when needed.
note: Written in 1513 and printed after his death in 1532; books cite both years.

name: Leviathan
summary: Argues that people in a state of nature, a war of all against all, contract to obey an absolute sovereign who keeps the peace.

name: Two Treatises of Government
summary: Rejects divine-right monarchy and grounds limited government in consent, to protect life, liberty and property.
note: Printed in late 1689 with 1690 on the title page; books cite both years.
verified: books: Heywood; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: The Social Contract
summary: Holds that legitimate authority comes from a contract that makes the people sovereign under the general will.

name: On Liberty
summary: Defends freedom of thought, expression and action, allowing interference only to prevent harm to others.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: The Communist Manifesto
aliases: Manifesto of the Communist Party|Communist Manifesto
summary: Pamphlet declaring that all history is the history of class struggles and calling on workers to overthrow capitalism.
note: Co-written with Friedrich Engels.

name: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism
aliases: Imperialism: The Highest Stage of Capitalism
summary: Explains imperialism as monopoly capitalism that exports capital and divides the world among the great powers.
note: Written in 1916, published in 1917.
verified: books: Baylis & Smith; Heywood; O.P. Gauba

name: Prison Notebooks
aliases: Selections from the Prison Notebooks|Quaderni del carcere
summary: Notes written in a fascist prison that develop hegemony, civil and political society, passive revolution and organic intellectuals.
note: Written 1929-1935 and published after his death: in Italian from 1948, in an English selection in 1971.

name: The Origins of Totalitarianism
summary: Traces Nazi and Stalinist totalitarianism to antisemitism, imperialism and mass society, and to rule by terror and ideology.

name: A Theory of Justice
summary: Derives two principles of justice, equal basic liberties and inequalities only to the benefit of the least advantaged, from an original position.
verified: books: Heywood; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: Anarchy, State, and Utopia
summary: Defends a minimal state and an entitlement theory: holdings justly acquired or transferred are just, so redistribution violates rights.

name: The Idea of Justice
summary: Rejects the search for a perfectly just society and compares real outcomes, contrasting niti with nyaya.

name: Spheres of Justice
summary: Argues for complex equality, in which each social good is distributed within its own sphere by its own social meaning.

name: Two Concepts of Liberty
summary: Lecture that separates negative liberty from positive liberty and warns that positive liberty can be used to justify coercion.
note: Oxford inaugural lecture of 1958, reprinted in Four Essays on Liberty in 1969.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy
summary: Redefines democracy as a method in which leaders gain power by competing for the people's vote.

name: The Political System
summary: Calls for a general theory of politics and defines politics as the authoritative allocation of values for a society.

name: The Civic Culture
summary: Five-nation survey that sorts political culture into parochial, subject and participant types and links a mixed civic culture to stable democracy.
note: Co-written with Sidney Verba.

name: Power: A Radical View
summary: Argues that power has three dimensions: decision-making, agenda-setting, and shaping people's wants and beliefs.

name: The Road to Serfdom
summary: Warns that central economic planning leads to the loss of freedom and to totalitarianism.

name: A Grammar of Politics
summary: Argues for a pluralist state that shares authority with associations and treats rights as the conditions of self-development.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: The Second Sex
summary: Argues that one is not born but becomes a woman, as society makes woman man's Other.
note: French original 1949, English translation 1953.

name: Politics Among Nations
summary: Classical realist text holding that international politics is a struggle for power and that states act on interest defined as power.

name: The Twenty Years' Crisis, 1919-1939
summary: Criticises interwar utopianism and argues that sound thinking about world politics must combine realism and utopia.

name: Theory of International Politics
summary: Founds neorealism: anarchy and the distribution of capabilities shape state behaviour, and a bipolar system is the most stable.

name: The Tragedy of Great Power Politics
summary: Sets out offensive realism: in anarchy great powers maximise relative power and aim at regional hegemony.

name: Power and Interdependence
summary: Sets out complex interdependence against realism: multiple channels between societies, no hierarchy of issues and a minor role for military force.
note: Co-written with Joseph Nye.

name: Anarchy is What States Make of It
summary: Article arguing that self-help and power politics do not follow from anarchy but from identities and interests that states construct.

name: The End of History and the Last Man
summary: Argues that liberal democracy may be the end point of humanity's ideological evolution.
note: Grew out of his 1989 essay 'The End of History?' in The National Interest.

name: Hind Swaraj
summary: Dialogue that condemns modern Western civilisation and defines true swaraj as self-rule through non-violence.
note: Written in Gujarati in 1909; the English translation appeared in 1910.

name: Annihilation of Caste
summary: Undelivered speech that attacks caste and its basis in the Hindu shastras and calls for its destruction.

name: The Causes of the Indian Revolt
summary: Argues that the revolt of 1857 arose because the British misunderstood Indians and kept them out of the Legislative Council.
note: Written in 1858 and published in 1859; books cite both years.

name: The Doctrine of Passive Resistance
summary: Articles arguing for organised passive resistance through boycott and swadeshi, while allowing force against violent repression.
note: First published as articles in Bande Mataram in 1907.

name: Social Background of Indian Nationalism
summary: Marxist account of Indian nationalism as a product of the economic and class changes brought by British rule.

name: The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation
summary: History of the Constituent Assembly showing how it built the Constitution through consensus and accommodation.

name: Philosopher-king
summary: Plato's ideal ruler, who knows the Good through reason and rules the just state without private property or family.

name: Saptanga theory
summary: Kautilya's theory that the state has seven elements: swami, amatya, janapada, durga, kosha, danda and mitra.

name: Mandala theory
summary: Kautilya's circle of states, in which a neighbouring state is a natural enemy and the state beyond it a natural ally.

name: Dharmashastra
summary: Brahmanical texts such as the Manusmriti that make protecting dharma and the varna order the king's duty, or rajadharma.

name: Mahasammata
summary: Buddhist idea, from the Agganna Sutta, that the people chose the first king to keep order: an early contract theory.

name: Sovereignty
summary: Supreme and final legal authority of the state over its territory and people, systematised by Bodin and developed by Hobbes and Austin.
verified: books: IGNOU Political Science Paper 1; O.P. Gauba

name: General will
summary: Rousseau's idea of the will of the sovereign people aimed at the common good, as distinct from the will of all.

name: Harm principle
summary: Mill's principle that power may be used over anyone against their will only to prevent harm to others.

name: Historical materialism
summary: Marx's view that the mode of production is the base on which law, politics and ideas rise as a superstructure.

name: Hegemony
summary: Gramsci's idea that a ruling class rules by winning the consent of the ruled through civil society, not by force alone.
note: In IR the word also means a dominant state's leadership, which is not Gramsci's sense.

name: Three types of authority
aliases: Types of legitimate authority|Weber's types of legitimacy
summary: Weber's three types of legitimate domination: traditional, charismatic and legal-rational authority.

name: Negative and positive liberty
summary: Berlin's distinction between freedom from interference by others and freedom as self-mastery or self-rule.

name: Original position
summary: Rawls's hypothetical choice in which people pick principles of justice behind a veil of ignorance about their own place in society.

name: Capability approach
summary: Judges well-being and justice by what people are actually able to do and to be, not by income or resources alone.
note: Also developed by Martha Nussbaum.

name: Polyarchy
summary: Dahl's term for real-world democracies, marked by wide participation and open public contestation among competing groups.

name: Deliberative democracy
summary: Model in which democratic legitimacy comes from free and equal public reasoning among citizens, not only from voting.
note: Joseph Bessette coined the term in 1980; Habermas is its leading theorist.

name: Behaviouralism
summary: Approach that dominated American political science in the 1950s and 1960s, studying observable behaviour with scientific, value-free methods.

name: Post-behaviouralism
summary: Easton's call for relevance and action, bringing values and urgent social problems back into political science.
note: Announced in Easton's 1969 presidential address to the American Political Science Association.

name: Duverger's law
summary: The simple-majority single-ballot system tends to produce a two-party system; proportional representation tends to favour many parties.

name: Congress system
summary: Kothari's account of Congress as a dominant party of consensus, with opposition parties acting as a margin of pressure.

name: Balance of power
summary: Distribution of power among states such that no single state can dominate the rest; a core realist idea.

name: National interest
summary: The goals a state pursues abroad; Morgenthau's realism defines them as interest in terms of power.
verified: books: Heywood; IGNOU Political Science Paper 2

name: Security dilemma
summary: Situation in which one state's measures for its own security make others feel less secure, leading to arms races.
note: John Herz coined the term in 1950; Herbert Butterfield described the same idea in 1951.

name: Collective security
summary: Arrangement in which all states agree to act together against any aggressor, as under the League Covenant and Chapter VII of the UN Charter.

name: Soft power
summary: Ability to get what one wants through the attraction of culture, values and policies rather than coercion or payment.
note: Coined in Nye's Bound to Lead (1990).

name: Neorealism
summary: Realism that explains state behaviour by the anarchic structure of the international system and the distribution of capabilities.

name: Constructivism
summary: Approach holding that international structures are social, made of shared ideas, norms and identities rather than material power alone.
note: Nicholas Onuf brought the term into IR in 1989; Wendt is its best-known theorist.

name: World-systems theory
summary: Sees one capitalist world-economy divided into core, semi-periphery and periphery, with surplus flowing to the core.

name: Dependency theory
summary: Holds that developing countries stay underdeveloped because of unequal ties to the industrial core; associated with Prebisch and Andre Gunder Frank.

name: Functionalism
summary: Mitrany's view that peace grows from international agencies built around shared practical tasks rather than political federation.

name: Clash of civilizations
summary: Huntington's thesis that after the Cold War the main conflicts would run along cultural fault lines between civilizations.
note: Foreign Affairs article 1993, expanded into a book in 1996.

name: Satyagraha
summary: Gandhi's method of resisting injustice by truth and non-violence, aiming to convert the opponent through self-suffering.
verified: books: Heywood; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: Trusteeship
summary: Gandhi's idea that the rich should hold their wealth in trust and use it for the good of society.

name: Radical humanism
summary: Roy's philosophy that puts the free individual, reason and morality at the centre of politics instead of class or nation.

name: Basic structure doctrine
summary: Supreme Court doctrine, laid down in Kesavananda Bharati, that Parliament can amend the Constitution but not destroy its basic structure.

name: Quasi-federal
summary: Wheare's view of the Indian Constitution as a unitary state with subsidiary federal features rather than a federal state with unitary features.

name: Cooperative federalism
summary: Austin's description of Indian federalism: a strong Centre that does not weaken the states but works together with them.
note: Austin applied the term to India; it was in use earlier for other federations.

name: Non-alignment
summary: India's policy of staying out of Cold War military blocs while keeping the freedom to judge each issue on its merits.
note: The word is often credited to V. K. Krishna Menon.

name: Gujral Doctrine
summary: Five principles under which India gives smaller neighbours what it can without asking for reciprocity, with non-interference and peaceful settlement.

name: Responsibility to Protect
summary: Norm that each state must protect its people from genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity, and others may act if it fails.
note: Proposed by the ICISS report in 2001; endorsed at the 2005 UN World Summit.

name: Founding of the Indian National Congress
summary: First session met in Bombay under W. C. Bonnerjee with 72 delegates; A. O. Hume helped found it.

name: Non-Cooperation Movement
summary: Gandhi's first all-India mass movement, joined with the Khilafat cause and called off after the violence at Chauri Chaura.

name: Civil Disobedience Movement
summary: Mass breaking of colonial laws that began with Gandhi's Dandi March against the salt law in March 1930.

name: Quit India Movement
summary: The AICC passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay with Gandhi's call of 'Do or Die'; leaders were arrested the next day.
note: Resolution passed 8 August 1942; the arrests on 9 August are often given as the start.

name: Objectives Resolution
summary: Resolution moved by Nehru in the Constituent Assembly that set out the Constitution's ideals and later became the basis of the Preamble.
note: Moved on 13 December 1946, adopted on 22 January 1947.

name: Adoption of the Constitution of India
summary: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution, which came into force on 26 January 1950.
note: Adopted 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day); in force 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

name: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
summary: Gave constitutional status to panchayats, adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule and reserving one-third of seats for women.
note: In force from 24 April 1993.

name: 74th Constitutional Amendment Act
summary: Gave constitutional status to urban local bodies, adding Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule.
note: In force from 1 June 1993.

name: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
summary: Recommended democratic decentralisation through a three-tier panchayati raj of village, block and district bodies.

name: Sarkaria Commission
summary: Commission on Centre-state relations that backed a strong Centre but urged sparing use of Article 356 and a permanent Inter-State Council.
note: Set up in 1983; it reported in 1988.

name: Mandal Commission
summary: Commission under B. P. Mandal that recommended 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes in central government jobs.
note: Set up 1979, reported 1980; the V. P. Singh government implemented it in 1990.

name: NITI Aayog
summary: Policy think tank that replaced the Planning Commission to promote cooperative federalism, without the power to allocate funds.

name: National Human Rights Commission
summary: Statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993 that inquires into violations of human rights.

name: Signing of the UN Charter
aliases: Charter of the United Nations|UN Charter
summary: Fifty states, India among them, signed the Charter at the San Francisco Conference, founding the United Nations.
note: In force 24 October 1945, now UN Day.

name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: Adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris as a common standard of civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.
verified: books: Baylis & Smith; IGNOU Political Science Paper 1

name: Bretton Woods Conference
summary: Conference of 44 Allied nations in New Hampshire that created the IMF and the World Bank and a system of fixed exchange rates.

name: Establishment of the World Trade Organization
summary: The WTO replaced GATT as the body for global trade rules, created by the Marrakesh Agreement after the Uruguay Round.

name: Declaration on the Establishment of a New International Economic Order
summary: UN General Assembly declaration, pushed by developing countries, for fairer trade, sovereignty over resources and reform of the world economy.

name: Panchsheel Agreement
summary: India-China agreement on trade with the Tibet region whose preamble set out the five principles of peaceful coexistence.

name: Bandung Conference
summary: Meeting of 29 Asian and African states in Indonesia that adopted ten principles and prepared the ground for non-alignment.

name: First NAM Summit, Belgrade
summary: First summit of the Non-Aligned Movement with 25 member states, led by Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah.

name: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
summary: Treaty that recognises five nuclear-weapon states; India refused to sign it as discriminatory.
note: Opened for signature 1 July 1968; in force 5 March 1970.

name: Pokhran-I
summary: India's first nuclear test, described by the government as a peaceful nuclear explosion.

name: Pokhran-II
summary: Five nuclear tests on 11 and 13 May 1998, after which India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state.

name: India's Nuclear Doctrine
summary: Doctrine of credible minimum deterrence and no first use, with massive retaliation under civilian political control.
note: A draft doctrine was released in August 1999.

name: India-US Civil Nuclear Agreement
summary: The signed 123 Agreement opened civil nuclear trade with India outside the NPT, after a Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver in September 2008.
note: Began with the joint statement of 18 July 2005; books date the deal 2005 or 2008.

name: Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation
summary: Twenty-year treaty signed months before the Bangladesh war, giving India Soviet support against the US-China-Pakistan alignment.

name: Simla Agreement
summary: Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto agreed to settle disputes bilaterally and turned the Kashmir ceasefire line into the Line of Control.

name: Founding of SAARC
aliases: SAARC|South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
summary: Seven South Asian states founded SAARC at Dhaka; Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

name: Act East Policy
summary: Upgrade of the Look East Policy announced in 2014, adding security, connectivity and the wider Indo-Pacific to economic ties.
note: Look East is usually dated 1991, under P. V. Narasimha Rao.

name: Paris Agreement
summary: Climate treaty under the UNFCCC in which every party sets nationally determined contributions to hold warming well below 2°C.
note: In force from 4 November 2016.
